The 1st Brigade headquarters now sits 50 km from the border and a base for 1,000 troops is being built in Narva, to 'keep the war away from Estonian territory'; the same moves put the main force within Russian reach and are exactly the target a provocation-to-test-Article-5 would choose.

grand_strategy.reading: Estonia runs the grand strategy of a front-line state that has decided to spend its way to being un-attackable rather than hope for a guarantor: 5.43% of GDP, a fortified border, a deep-strike arsenal and a dense net of partners (UK, Finland, Poland, Germany, Korea) around an American umbrella it publicly trusts and privately hedges. The Luttwak pattern is that each hardening has a cost that returns on the same front: the forward posture raises exposure, enforcement at sea shows the limits of the law, grid independence concentrates risk in cables, and the defence of the nation-state against Russian leverage on the minority hands Moscow a grievance narrative. Russia is graded a rival, not an adversary: Estonia seeks deterrence, a Russian defeat in Ukraine and a Russia that pays, not the end of the Russian state, and keeps an embassy and a border regime open. The Kremlin's line that Russia 'poses no threat' to Estonia and the Estonian intelligence judgement that Moscow has no intention of attacking in the coming year are signals, not rows: both sides are reading the other's limits. The open question for 2027 is the American presence after the end-2026 rotation and an election that a weak coalition may lose.

stances.note: Rival, not adversary: Estonia's aim is deterrence, a Russian defeat in Ukraine and payment of damages, not the end of the Russian state or its regime; it keeps a border regime and diplomatic contact (chargé d'affaires summoned). The friction is the sharpest in the Baltic: MiG-31 intrusion and Article 4 request (19 Sep 2025), the Jaguar/Su-35 episode (May 2025), GPS jamming, the Milrem arson blamed on Russian services (Sep 2026), the Estlink 2 cut. Estonian foreign intelligence calls Russia the main threat but judges it has no intention to attack in the coming year; the Kremlin says it poses no threat to Estonia. No source uses 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), and Moscow's side (RUS card) is expected to grade Estonia more harshly - an asymmetric pair that is deliberate. Bond - grievance: the Soviet occupation and Russian claim to protect Russian speakers.
